stories.headline: OpenAI reportedly plans to buy Google AI chips
stories.summary: The Information reports OpenAI plans to purchase Google's AI chips, potentially broadening its compute supply beyond Nvidia. Terms were not disclosed; OpenAI declined comment and Google had not responded, so the purchase remains unconfirmed.

stories.headline: China's CXMT plans AI memory despite low yields
stories.summary: Sources say CXMT aims for limited HBM3E production within two months despite only 20–30% usable output. This could ease China's AI-memory shortage, but the yield and timing claims are unconfirmed; CXMT did not comment.

stories.headline: Judge finds LA's top federal prosecutor unlawful
stories.summary: A federal judge ruled Bill Essayli is unlawfully serving as Los Angeles's de facto US attorney. The order is not yet effective while a stay request is considered; Essayli disputes the ruling and expects further appeals.

stories.headline: Israel election leaves rival blocs short of majority
stories.summary: Early counting left both Netanyahu's and Eisenkot's blocs below the 61 seats needed to govern. Projections may change as counting continues; neither side has a confirmed coalition or clear victory.

stories.headline: Oil rises after claimed Saudi refinery strike
stories.summary: Oil rose after the Houthis claimed a missile strike on Saudi Arabia's largest refinery. Saudi authorities had not confirmed the attack; disruption and damage remain uncertain despite renewed market concern over supply.
